author: Abahlali_3
title: We Welcome the President’s Response to Femicide, but Much More Must Be Done
content:
1 October 2026 Abahlali baseMjondolo Women’s League Press Statement

We Welcome the President’s Response to Femicide, but Much More Must Be Done

On 28 September 2026, after 11 women had been murdered in Ekurhuleni since July, Abahlali baseMjondolo and other residents of Ekurhuleni marched in Kempton Park against the killing of women and the failure of the police to adequately protect women from violence. We handed a memorandum to the Kempton Park Police Station and Ekurhuleni District Management.

•⁠ ⁠A public report on the investigations into the 11 murders, presented at an open public meeting. •⁠ ⁠A well-funded and properly equipped women-led GBV task team for the townships and shack settlements of Ekurhuleni. •⁠ ⁠A 24-hour Victim Support Room at Kempton Park Police Station with properly trained female officers. •⁠ ⁠Daily visible and women-friendly policing in high-risk areas, with additional patrols at night and on weekends. •⁠ ⁠A public audit of all GBV cases reported in Ekurhuleni since July. •⁠ ⁠An open public meeting at which the police must account to the women of Ekurhuleni for failures in responding to GBV and femicide. •⁠ ⁠The election of a women’s committee to which the police must report every week on their work relating to GBV and femicide.

We therefore welcome much of what President Cyril Ramaphosa announced in his address to the nation on 29 September.

author: Abahlali_3
title: Memorandum to the Station Commander at the Kempton Park Police Station
content:
MEMORANDUM TO THE STATION COMMANDER

From: Abahlali baseMjondolo & Ekurhuleni Community

DEMAND FOR URGENT ACTION ON FEMICIDE IN EKURHULENI

SAPS KEMPTON PARK AND EKURHULENI DISTRICT MANAGEMENT

We, the residents of Ekurhuleni, women, and members of Abahlali baseMjondolo, bring this memorandum with heavy hearts and deep anger.

Since July 2026, 11 women have been murdered in Ekurhuleni in GBV-related incidents. Many more have been raped, assaulted and threatened. Our communities live in fear. Women cannot walk at night, cannot work late shifts and cannot even sleep in our shacks without fear.

•⁠ ⁠GBV cases are not taken seriously when opened. Victims are sent from pillar to post.

•⁠ ⁠Protection orders are not enforced.

•⁠ ⁠Dockets disappear and no feedback is given to families.

•⁠ ⁠Police response time in shack settlements is extremely slow.

•⁠ ⁠Women who report are not protected.

•⁠ ⁠Women who report are often not treated with dignity by the police.

Section 12 of the Constitution guarantees everyone the right to be free from violence. Section 205 says SAPS has the duty to prevent crime and protect inhabitants. The police in Ekurhuleni are failing in their duty.

title: March Against the Separation Wall in Cape Town
content:
4 September 2024 Abahlali baseMjondolo press statement

March Against the Separation Wall in Cape Town

Today thousands of people are marching in the street of Cape Town against the building of a separation wall that repeats the logic of apartheid spatial segregation.

The City of Cape Town continues to entrench neo-apartheid laws in post apartheid South Africa by building a wall that segregates and hides the poor from the rich along the N2.

This wall is sign that the City of Cape Town under the Democratic Alliance does not recognise the poor, who are black in particular. The DA has always introduced and favoured laws that are anti-poor and anti-black.

Abahlali baseMjondolo supports the struggles of the people of Cape Town who continue to face segregation and racism under the DA led municipality. We support the march that is taking place today against this act of hatred and undermining of the poor in Khayeltsha, Langa, Dunoon and Gugulethu and Mitchels Plain. We will not support neo-apartheid segregation.
